findings.excerpt: rwa [FinitePointBlowup.point_support q S.structureMap hq j] at hk
findings.problem: The same three-line argument is written twice. `change _ ∈ ((q j).ker.support : Set S.scheme) at _` followed by `rwa [point_support ...]` turns support membership into equality with the rational point. It is used once for `hxj` (lines 40-42) and once for `hyj` (lines 60-62). Each copy repeats the `change` coercion boilerplate and the long `FinitePointBlowup.point_support` argument list.
findings.proposed_change: Before `by_cases`, state the fact once, for example `have hsupp : ∀ k z, z ∈ (q k).ker.support → z = q k (fieldPoint ℂ) := fun k z hz => by change z ∈ ((q k).ker.support : Set S.scheme) at hz; rwa [FinitePointBlowup.point_support q S.structureMap hq k] at hz`. Then use `have hxj := hsupp j x hj` and `have hyj := hsupp j y hk`. This removes both `have ... := by change ...; rwa ...` blocks. The `hkj`/`subst` step can likewise become `obtain rfl : k = j := by_contra fun hne => ...`, or stay as it is.
findings.benefit: The proof states the one key fact, that support of a centre is the single point, once and by name. Each use becomes a one-line application, and the `change`/`rwa` boilerplate is not duplicated. A reader no longer has to compare two copies to check they are identical.

findings.problem: The trivial line bundle structure `⟨O S.scheme, fun _ => ⟨⊤, trivial, ⟨Scheme.Modules.restrictUnitIso _⟩⟩⟩` is written out in full in both branches (lines 43 and 66). The same anonymous constructor is also written out in BlowupLineDescent.lean as `OY`. The long anonymous-constructor term hides the fact that it is just the structure sheaf viewed as a line bundle. It also pushes the two `obtain` lines far past the line width.
findings.proposed_change: Bind it once at the top of the proof, next to `q`, `hq` and `hd`: `let J : LineBundle S.scheme := ⟨O S.scheme, fun _ => ⟨⊤, trivial, ⟨Scheme.Modules.restrictUnitIso _⟩⟩⟩`. Then write `obtain ⟨U,hxU,hUW,e,t,het⟩ := S.etale_line_frame_inside J (W ⊓ ...) x ...` in both branches. A better option is a named `LineBundle.unit` definition in the library, shared with BlowupLineDescent.lean's `OY`. The unused frame `e` could also become `_`.
findings.benefit: The two calls then read as the same chart lookup with two different open sets. The line-bundle boilerplate is separated from the mathematics, and a later change to the construction touches one place.
